Tax & Business Advisory Accountant
 
Looking for a firm that's invested in your future? We've Got Your Back.
Great accountants don't just prepare tax returns—they change lives.
At EnVision Partners, we believe accounting is about far more than numbers.
It's about helping business owners make better decisions, reduce stress, grow their wealth and create a legacy for future generations.


That's why our promise to every client—and every member of our team—is simple: We've Got Your Back.
As our business continues to grow, we're looking for an Accountant or Senior Accountant who wants more than a job. We're looking for someone who wants to build trusted relationships, challenge themselves professionally and be part of a team that's shaping the future of regional business.
Whether you're based in Chinchilla or anywhere across Queensland, we'd love to hear from you.


Why Join EnVision Partners?
We know you have options. So why choose EnVision? Because here, you're more than another employee.
You'll join a team that genuinely supports one another, values new ideas and believes your career should be just as important as the success of our clients.


What you'll enjoy:
✔ An attractive salary package based on your experience
✔ Flexible working arrangements, including remote work opportunities throughout Queensland
✔ A supportive and friendly team culture where We've Got Your Back isn't just a slogan—it's how we work every day
✔ The opportunity to work directly alongside experienced leaders and influence the future direction of the firm
✔ Ongoing mentoring, professional development and genuine career progression
✔ Exposure to business advisory, strategic planning and value-added client work—not just compliance
✔ A diverse client portfolio across retail, commercial, primary production, investment and professional services
✔ A workplace that embraces innovation, cloud technology and AI to help us deliver even better outcomes
✔ Modern systems that allow you to spend more time advising clients and less time on administration


What You'll Be Doing
You'll become a trusted adviser to a portfolio of clients, helping them navigate every stage of their business journey.


Your work will include:

- Preparing financial statements and tax returns
- Preparing BAS and IAS
- Tax planning and compliance advice
- Assisting with business structures and strategic planning
- Budgeting, forecasting and cash flow management
- Working closely with business owners to identify opportunities for growth
- Building long-term client relationships
- Working with Xero and cloud-based accounting systems
- Liaising with the Australian Taxation Office


You'll Thrive Here If You...
We're not looking for someone who's simply good with numbers.
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people.
You'll fit right in if you:

- Enjoy building lasting client relationships.
- Like solving problems and thinking beyond compliance.
- Want to be part of a supportive, high-performing team.
- Take pride in producing quality work.
- Embrace technology and continuous improvement.
- Are curious, motivated and always looking to learn.
- Believe that great client service starts with genuinely caring.


About You
You'll ideally have:

- A Bachelor of Accounting or related qualification
- CPA or CA qualification (or working towards it)
- Experience within public practice accounting
- Strong knowledge of Australian taxation legislation
- Experience preparing financial statements and tax returns
- Experience using Xero
- Excellent communication skills
- Outstanding attention to detail
- Strong organisational and time management skills


About EnVision Partners
EnVision Partners is more than an accounting firm. We're trusted advisers, problem solvers and partners in our clients' success. We provide accounting, taxation, bookkeeping, business advisory and strategic planning services to businesses across a broad range of industries. Our people are the reason for our success. We invest in them, support them and celebrate their achievements because we know that when our team succeeds, our clients succeed too.


Why Chinchilla?
Thinking about a tree change? Chinchilla offers the lifestyle many professionals are searching for.
Imagine:

- Being at work in five minutes instead of sitting in traffic.
- Enjoying affordable housing and a strong sense of community.
- Having more time for family, hobbies and the things that matter most.
- Building a rewarding career without sacrificing work-life balance.
Not planning to relocate? No problem. We're also open to exceptional candidates located anywhere within Queensland who can work remotely.


And Finally...
We believe work should be enjoyable. You'll find plenty of laughs, daily morning teas, birthday cake, genuine friendships and a team that's always willing to help. Because at EnVision Partners...
We've Got Your Back.


How to Apply
As attention to detail is one of the most important qualities for this role, we won't be accepting applications from anyone who simply clicks "Apply Now" on SEEK or sends through a generic application.
We're looking for someone who reads the details, follows instructions and takes pride in doing things properly.

Business Made Simple | When Complexity Requires a Clear Explanation

Are you running a growing business?  Do you feel that your financial and accounting decisions are becoming too great or complex for you to manage entirely yourself?  If you answered yes to either of these questions, you are not alone.  At some point, all businesses, families and individuals recognise the need to enlist the services of a dedicated accounting firm.

EnVision offers a selection of accounting and business services designed with regional people in mind.  Specialising in taxation strategy, bookkeeping best practice, estate planning, business management and personal insurance across all industries (specialisation in primary production); we serve customers who are committed and conscientious individuals seeking solutions to grow their wealth and opportunities.

EnVision Partners, located in the regional town of Chinchilla, but reaching customers in nearly all States and Territories of Australia, offers a uniquely warm and welcoming environment where we are committed to taking our customers beyond taxation compliance, partnering with them to 'Understand the impact of every decision before they make it'​.

Fully Remote Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager
Top 10 CPA Firm
Full-Time • $125,000–$195,000 base + Bonus (At least 20%)
Consistently pay out 100%+ of target bonus


About the Practice
This Top 10 CPA Firm's Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) group is a leading national due diligence practice supporting middle‑market private equity groups and companies. The team specializes in helping clients make informed investment decisions through high‑impact financial and operational analysis.


The practice has experienced significant growth, more than doubling in size over the past two years (currently sits at 40 employees) and is looking to hire a fully remote Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager.


What truly differentiates this team is its people‑first culture, entrepreneurial mindset, and commitment to real work‑life balance.


Why candidates are excited about this role:

- Fully remote with minimal travel
- Market‑leading compensation + strong bonus potential
- Manager: $125,000 - $155,000 Base + 20% Bonus (twenty percent is the floor)
- Senior Manager: $155,000 - $195,000 Base + 25% Bonus (twenty-five percent is the floor)
- Predictable schedules and genuine respect for personal time
- 40 to 45-hour work week
- Direct client exposure and long‑term relationship building
- Leadership support, growth opportunities, and merit‑based promotions


About the Role
The Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager will support private equity groups and companies through both buy‑side and sell‑side financial due diligence engagements. You will analyze target company financials, identify risks and opportunities, and provide insights that influence valuation, deal structure, and strategic decisions.


Preferred Qualifications

- CPA (or CPA‑eligible); strong understanding of U.S. GAAP.
- Master’s in Accounting or MBA with accounting undergrad preferred.
- 2–4+ years of financial audit experience (ideally with a top‑ten public accounting firm).
- 1–3 years in a TAS practice at a national accounting firm, including at least 1 year at the Manager level.
- Excellent communication skills — written and verbal.
- Advanced Excel skills; strong MS Office proficiency.
- Self‑driven, entrepreneurial, and able to thrive in a fast‑paced environment.


About the Organization
The broader organization is a nationally recognized professional services platform supporting middle‑market businesses across accounting, tax, advisory, benefits, insurance, and technology. With 10,000+ team members across 160+ U.S. locations, the company provides forward‑thinking insights and impactful client solutions.

job_description:
At Common Trust, we're on a mission to make employee ownership the norm, not the exception. We help business owners sell their businesses to their employees, creating shared prosperity that strengthens companies, communities, and the broader economy. Common Trust has worked with businesses that have enabled over 63,000 workers to become employee-owners to date with a 93% client satisfaction rating, but for us, this is just the beginning.


With 75% of all business owners in the US looking to sell over the next decade, we believe that making employee ownership the transition of choice for small businesses is one of the most powerful ways for business owners to transition competitively, close the wealth gap in America, and build an economy worthy of passing on to the next generation. In this role, you'll be at the center of working with the business owners making it happen.


Learn more about us: Common-Trust.com




Position Summary


In response to growing demand, our advisory team is now hiring a Transaction Advisory Manager to guide small and mid-sized business owners through the sale of their businesses to their employees.


Reporting to the Chief Client Services Officer, you'll partner closely with clients to help them understand the financial, tax, estate, governance, and long-term business implications of an employee ownership transition. You'll prepare financial analyses, facilitate client discussions, and build trusted relationships that support a smooth and successful ownership transition.


This is a remote position that can be based anywhere in the United States. We work across multiple U.S. time zones and gather in person several times each year for team meetings and occasional industry events.


While we are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious individual who has strong foundational knowledge in business, legal, and financial matters, we are pleased to provide structured on-boarding and training to build fluency in employee ownership structures and Common Trust’s advisory approach.




Key Responsibilities



- Guide business owners through the process to sell their business to their employees, including analyzing the opportunities and risks associated with the sale, evaluating the sale proceeds, estate impact, tax outcomes, decision-making and governance, long-term company stability, and employee benefits alongside the client’s corporate counsel where relevant.
- Develop and maintain financial models to evaluate transaction structures, operating forecasts, financing alternatives, cash flow generation, debt repayment capacity, and scenario analyses that support client decision-making and long-term ownership transition planning.
- Translate complex information regarding financial, legal, estate, and tax matters in terms that clients can understand so they can make values-aligned decisions.
- Collaborate with and project manage trust, estate, and corporate attorneys to ensure clients receive the best legal advice and their goals are integrated into the legal documentation for the transaction.
- Collaborate with clients’ accounting and tax professionals to ensure clients receive thorough and actionable guidance with respect to the employee ownership sale and post-sale tax outcomes.
- Facilitate employee engagement meetings to help employees understand the impact of the employee ownership sale.
- Prepare clear, decision-oriented client deliverables, including financial models, scenario analyses, and recommendations that synthesize goals, risks, tradeoffs, and key transaction and governance terms.
- Build long-term, trusted client relationships.
- Contribute to our company culture of continuous learning by ensuring that learnings about our clients are captured and shared across the organization, and with company support, pursuing your own individual learning and development in your role. We view learning, feedback and growth as shared responsibilities.




Education and Experience



- Education in business, finance, entrepreneurship, public policy, sustainability, or a related program is a plus, however we place equal value on relevant work experience that demonstrates the skills and character traits needed to be successful in this role
- 3+ years of experience in a client-facing advisory role navigating complex business, legal, and/or financial decisions; such as in any of the following: corporate finance, corporate development, valuation, wealth management, financial services, management consulting, or paralegal with a particular focus on corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions for small and mid-sized businesses, and/or trust and estate law
- Experience developing multi-year operating forecasts, cash flow projections, financing models, or transaction analyses for privately held businesses is a plus
- First-hand experience (either personal or professional) that provides a knowledgeable and compassionate understanding of the decisions a business owner will face when they are ready to transition out of owning their company is a plus
- Experience building scalable systems and processes in an early-stage, entrepreneurial environment is a plus




Skills and Character Traits



- Strong attention to detail when dealing with complex legal and tax information and comfort with distilling the implications of such information for a range of audiences
- Advanced financial modeling skills, including the ability to build and modify integrated operating, cash flow, financing, and scenario models to evaluate transaction structures and long-term business performance
- Strong understanding of corporate finance principles, including cash flow forecasting, debt financing, capital structure, valuation, and financial statement analysis
- Advanced Excel skills, including experience building dynamic financial models
- Ability to translate complex financial analyses into practical recommendations for business owners and other non-financial stakeholders
- Ability to build authentic and trusted relationships with small business owners, senior leaders, and workers of various backgrounds across the U.S.
- Excellent organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, timelines, and workstreams simultaneously
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, including comfort communicating complex legal, corporate governance, and financial topics to an audience that may not be familiar with technical financial or legal language
- Adaptability and willingness to work on a small team and take on the range of tasks necessary to deliver a high-quality product to clients, solve hard problems, and take initiative in improving processes
- Comfort working in a fast-paced, remote environment
- Proactive communication style, including the ability to manage up and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned on progress, risks, and next steps
- Interest in learning how to integrate new technologies into our workflows, including AI
- Passion for our mission to build a more prosperous and competitive economy through shared ownership




Why Join Our Mission


Our clients are inspiring and successful small business owners. Our clients are industry agnostic, located anywhere in the US, and range from $300,000 to $5M+ in EBITDA. Most business owners launched their company 20+ years ago, have a strong track record of profitability, and want to reward their long-term employees who helped build the successful business.


You will join a small, elite team with opportunity to make a real impact. Common Trust has approximately 10-15 employees, and the advisory team currently includes three incredibly talented, dynamic individuals who are shaping the way we do business. Two members of the advisory team have been with the company since its founding, and every member of the team has driven key innovations that are helping us scale our work while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction. We are seeking another dynamo who wants to help us learn and improve the way we work, with plenty of opportunity for innovation and sharing ideas!


The work is hard and interesting. The Employee Ownership Trust structure was first utilized for business ownership in 2014, and is growing in popularity. Common Trust has been a key player in pioneering the structure, supporting businesses worth over $813M in aggregate to transition to EOT ownership. The work to uncover the efficiencies with respect to transaction structure, tax, and estate impacts that will help take this model to scale is not done!




What We Offer



- Opportunity to shape the future of business ownership in the U.S.
- A values-driven culture that prioritizes integrity, inclusion, and long-term thinking
- Compensation: $100,000 - $130,000 base salary, commensurate with experience; and an equity incentive plan


Benefits:

- Remote and flexible work schedule and environment
- Monthly coworking stipend + one-time home office stipend
- Health insurance: 99% medical and 50% vision/dental covered by employer
- 401(k) retirement plan
- Unlimited paid time off
- Paid parental leave plan




Equal Opportunity Employer


Common Trust provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, familial status, military status, height and weight, genetic predisposition or carrier status, arrest record, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. We strongly encourage people of color, people with disabilities, women, and LGBTQ candidates to apply.

Location: Australia
Work style: Full-time | Fully remote role


To be considered, you must currently reside in Australia and be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.


Why This Role
This is an opportunity for an experienced Senior Accountant to join a growing boutique accounting and advisory firm operating on a fully remote basis.


The role will suit someone who is technically strong, proactive, and confident in managing work without close supervision. You will be trusted to take ownership, communicate clearly and deliver high-quality work across tax, compliance and business services matters.


This is not a traditional suburban accounting role where the Partner reviews every detail before anything moves forward. The firm is looking for someone who can operate with care, judgement and accountability, while still having access to support when needed.


The role offers strong flexibility, broader client exposure and the opportunity to work in a firm that values responsiveness, commercial thinking and practical advice.


About Our Client
Our client is a boutique accounting and advisory firm supporting business owners, medical professionals, property investors and private clients.


The firm provides tax compliance, business advisory, structuring, cash flow support, SMSF and property-related advice.


The leadership team brings experience across Big 4 tax, international tax, mergers and acquisitions, strategy consulting and private client advisory. That background flows through to the firm's approach, which is focused on high-quality advice, responsiveness and helping clients make better commercial decisions.


The firm operates fully remotely, with regular team communication, daily check-ins, shared workflow lists, and modern systems that support collaboration across the team.


The Role
As a Senior Accountant, you will work across tax, accounting and business services matters for a diverse client base.


Your responsibilities will include:

- Preparing income tax returns for individuals, sole traders, companies, trusts and SMSFs
- Preparing financial statements and detailed working papers
- Preparing BAS and state tax returns, including payroll tax and land tax where required
- Preparing work through to review stage
- Researching tax issues and assisting with advice for senior team members and clients
- Liaising with the ATO, clients and other professionals
- Supporting tax planning and broader advisory work where appropriate
- Working with business owners, medical professionals, property investors and private clients
- Using Xero, Excel and other accounting systems to deliver accurate, timely work
- Contributing to process improvement as the firm continues to grow


This role is best suited to someone who wants to be hands-on, trusted and accountable, rather than someone who needs close supervision or prefers a heavily managed environment.


What You'll Bring

- At least 2+ years of experience in an Australian accounting firm
- Strong Senior Accountant-level capability across tax and business services
- Accounting degree from an Australian institution
- CA or CPA completed or underway
- Strong technical knowledge of Australian accounting and taxation fundamentals
- Experience preparing financial statements and tax returns for multiple entity types
- Strong Excel skills
- Experience with Xero
- Experience with MYOB AE, Logit or Karbon will be useful but is not essential
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to manage deadlines and workflow in a fully remote environment
- High attention to detail and strong professional judgement
- A proactive approach to solving problems before they escalate
- Australian citizenship or permanent residency


What's On Offer

- $100,000 to $115,000 + superannuation
- Fully remote role within Australia
- Career progression opportunities
- Paid professional association fees
- Regular professional development
- Direct access to experienced firm leadership
- Exposure to business owners, medical professionals and property investors
- Opportunity to build stronger advisory capability over time
- Modern remote working model with regular team communication
- Supportive boutique team environment
- A firm culture built around trust, autonomy, responsiveness and quality work


Next Steps
To apply, please submit your resume and academic transcript.
Applications without both documents may not be considered.

hello@minchinrecruitment.com.au
(07) 3733 3544

About the Job


Supervisor / Manager in a growing industry specialised firm (Brisbane based)
 
Newpoint Advisory (NA) provides financial analysis, restructuring and turnaround, and formal insolvency services to the property and construction industries across Australia. Our assignments range from distressed development and builder IAs to Builder Financial Reviews and Insolvency matters across property and builder restructures, property management and completion of distressed property developments.
 
NA’s core strategy is to help stakeholders mitigate risk and make informed credit and recovery decisions and is a trusted advisor to its clients, comprising secured lenders, developers and builders. For more information see NA’s website: www.newpointadvisory.com


This role suits a candidate with accounting / insolvency experience, who has a keen interest in the property and construction industries.
 
Qualifications and Experience Required:

- +4 years of insolvency and advisory experience including management of staff.
- Property and construction experience preferred, but not essential.
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Economics.
- CA/CPA qualified and willing to complete ARITA course (if not completed).
- Clear written and verbal communications skills.
- Commercial attitude to problem solving, negotiation and timely decisions.
- Motivated and efficient with an ability to take ownership of assigned matters and coordinate multiple work streams.
 
Tasks and Responsibilities:

- Part of the senior management team for business management and growth strategy.
- Workflow will generally include:
- Detailed financial modelling, forecast cashflow and feasibility analysis.
- Identify, analyse and implement strategic and creative options to maximise property realisations and outcomes across a range of distressed property types and locations.
- Coordinate lawyers, sales agents, builders, and other consultants to deliver target outcomes.
- Prepare reports for and engage with clients and creditors.
- Oversee statutory insolvency processes and procedures to mitigate risks.
- Staff management: mentor and develop staff and ensure achievement of required deadlines and quality expectations across multiple workstreams.
- Marketing: identify, formulate and support marketing efforts for existing clients and to secure new clients.
 
Why join NA:

- Growing team with collaborative working environment that encourages development of skills, service lines and clients.
- Flat structure with high autonomy and access to diverse industry client base.
- Training support and mentoring from a diversified team of professionals (finance, property, construction and insolvency).
- Option to work remotely.
- Access to high profile distressed property/construction projects across Eastern seaboard.
- Exposure to high-profile matters.
- Above market salary plus bonus potential.

Title: Integration Manager – M&A

Remote: Candidates in Eastern Time Zones

Supporting: IOA - Home Office (M&A Integration)

Requirements: Bachelors Degree in Business (or related field), 8-10 years P&C insurance experience managing a book

Please note: If this position is posted as either fully remote and/or hybrid, in accordance with company policy, individuals residing within a 50-mile radius of a branch location may be required to work onsite in a hybrid capacity as there may be occasions when on-site presence is necessary to meet specific business needs. Additionally, our remote work policy includes having a dedicated, distraction-free workspace. Remote work is not a substitute for childcare, elder care, or other personal responsibilities during working hours. To view our branch locations, please visit: ioausa.com/locations

About the Role: The Integration Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing merger and acquisition integration projects and large-scale transformation initiatives across the organization. This role serves as a key liaison between executive leadership, cross-functional teams, acquired entities, and external partners to ensure successful integration outcomes. The Integration Manager develops project frameworks, manages risks, tracks milestones, and drives organizational alignment to ensure initiatives remain on schedule, within budget, and aligned with strategic business objectives.

Key Responsibilities



- Integration Strategy & Planning: Define project objectives, integration roadmaps, timelines, success measures, and governance structures that support organizational goals. 
- Project Scope & Requirements: Collaborate with stakeholders to define project scope, establish objectives, identify dependencies, and ensure alignment with business priorities. 
- M&A Integration Leadership: Lead merger and acquisition integration initiatives, coordinating cross-functional workstreams to support successful business transitions. 
- Transformation Program Management: Oversee large-scale transformation projects, ensuring alignment of processes, systems, teams, and operational objectives. 
- Resource Coordination: Manage internal resources, third-party vendors, and project stakeholders to ensure appropriate allocation of support and capabilities. 
- Project Execution & Monitoring: Develop and maintain detailed project plans, monitor progress, and ensure milestones are achieved within established timelines and budgets. 
- Change Management: Manage project changes, scope adjustments, and implementation activities while maintaining stakeholder alignment and project integrity. 
- Risk Management: Identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and proactively address issues that may affect integration or transformation success. 
- Stakeholder Communication: Develop communication plans and provide regular updates to leadership regarding project status, risks, decisions, and outcomes. 
- Performance Measurement: Utilize project management tools, metrics, and reporting frameworks to evaluate progress and measure initiative success. 
- Documentation & Governance: Maintain comprehensive project documentation, integration plans, decision logs, and governance records throughout the project lifecycle. 
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with business leaders, operational teams, technology teams, Finance, HR, and external stakeholders to drive alignment and execution. 
- Process Improvement: Evaluate business processes, identify opportunities for operational enhancement, and implement scalable solutions that improve effectiveness and efficiency. 
- Leadership & Professional Development: Demonstrate effective project leadership while continuously strengthening project management and organizational change capabilities. 
- Champion IOA Values: Demonstrate integrity, leadership, accountability, and professionalism in all interactions. 

Ideal Candidate Qualifications



- Bachelor’s degree in Business or a related field required; MBA preferred 
- 8-10+ years of project management and P&C insurance experience 
- Experience leading M&A integrations, organizational transformations, or large-scale enterprise initiatives preferred 
- PMP certification preferred 
- Strong project management, organizational, and stakeholder management skills 
- Exceptional analytical, conceptual thinking, and problem-solving abilities 
- Proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple teams 
- Experience creating executive-level reports, presentations, and project documentation 
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook 
- Demonstrated success leading complex projects from planning through execution and delivery 
- Strong communication, prioritization, and time management skills 
- Proven leadership capability with a track record of driving results and managing competing priorities 

What We Offer



- Competitive salaries and bonus potential 
- Company-paid health insurance 
- Paid holidays, vacations, and sick time 
- 401K with employer match 
- Professional growth and career progression opportunities 
- Respectful culture and work/family life balance 
- Community service commitment 
- Supportive teammates and a rewarding work environment 

What To Expect (Application Process)



- 30-Minute Phone Screen, Online Assessments, and Interview(s). 

Salary Range

The expected pay range for this position is $100,000.00- $130,000.00 per year, depending on experience, relevant skills, and geographic location.

Insurance Office of America is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Top National Firm – Transaction Advisory Services Practice
Remote – U.S. Based


Manager - $125,000 - $155,000 w/ 20% Bonus (twenty percent is the floor, some high performing individuals see bonus up to and past 100%)


A top national professional services firm is continuing to expand its Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) practice, supporting middle‑market private equity groups and corporate buyers across the U.S. The TAS team specializes in financial due diligence for both buy‑side and sell‑side M&A transactions and has experienced significant, sustained growth over the last several years.


This group is known for its supportive leadership, collaborative culture, strong work‑life balance, and market‑leading compensation model. Team members work fully remote, enjoy minimal travel requirements, and have significant exposure to clients and leadership regardless of tenure. Promotions are merit‑based, not time‑based, creating real pathways for accelerated career progression.


If you are looking to join an entrepreneurial, high‑growth M&A due diligence team where your work has impact and your development is prioritized, this is an excellent opportunity.


What You’ll Do

- Lead and manage financial due diligence engagements for private equity and corporate clients.

Job Title: Financial Accountant
Company: Leading Healthcare Group (Confidential)
Location: 100% remote-based role! (CFO based in Melbourne so preference would based in VIC)
Remuneration: $80,000 – $85,000 + Super

About the Role

Supporting 500 clinicians across 6 healthcare brands, our client is a rapidly expanding healthcare group seeking a hands-on Financial Accountant. Acting as a key partner to the CFO, you will manage a service-based cost model focused on revenue, margin, and onshore/offshore salary structures. This position offers direct Board exposure, full ownership of month-end reporting and budgeting, and a dedicated technical oversight role across offshore operations.

Key Responsibilities

Month-End Close & Financial Reporting


- Own the month-end close calendar across all group entities, maintaining accuracy while working to optimize and reduce close timelines.
- Prepare monthly management accounts for individual entities and the consolidated group, including manual journals.
- Provide clear variance commentary against budget and forecast, explaining movements in commercial terms rather than purely accounting language.
- Review the monthly balance sheet reconciliation pack, implementing clear ageing and resolution plans for reconciling items.
- Prepare board and leadership reporting packs in conjunction with management, and support external audit processes.Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Analysis


- Coordinate and build annual budgets across all entities, establishing key assumptions with operational leaders.
- Maintain rolling financial and cash flow forecasts, highlighting timing risks and working capital pressures early.
- Contribute financial modelling and commercial analysis for pricing decisions, new service lines, and structural changes.Offshore Output Review & Quality Assurance


- Perform technical reviews on work delivered by 2 offshore finance team members, covering AP/AR, bank recs, clinician pay runs, onshore payroll support, and GL coding.
- Verify transactions are coded consistently against group accounting policies and the chart of accounts across all entities.
- Review bank, clearing, and control account reconciliations to ensure reconciling items are genuine and resolved promptly.
- Provide constructive, documented feedback and build process notes, checklists, and templates to lift output quality over time.
- Note: The offshore team is managed directly by the CFO. This role acts as a technical review function and does not carry line management responsibilities.Group Policy, Compliance & Controls


- Ensure correct and consistent accounting treatment compliant with Australian Accounting Standards (AASB) and internal policy.
- Maintain and update the group chart of accounts and procedure documentation as the business expands.Selection Criteria

Essential


- Education & Qualification: CA or CPA qualified (or currently completing studies), with a relevant degree in Accounting, Commerce, or Finance.
- Technical Experience: Strong core experience in financial accounting, month-end close, consolidated group reporting, and budgeting/forecasting.
- Systems & Excel: Advanced Excel skills (handling large data sets and building multi-entity financial models) and proficiency in Xero.
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, with an ability to translate complex financial results for non-finance stakeholders and clinicians.
- Mindset: Highly autonomous with a "roll up your sleeves" approach to balance detailed transactional review with high-level reporting.Desirable


- Prior experience in healthcare, allied health, clinical services, or NDIS environments.
- Experience working alongside or reviewing output from offshore/outsourced finance teams.
- Exposure to multi-entity groups undergoing rapid growth or restructuring.

We are seeking an Operations Manager to join a newly established, transaction-focused financial services business. You'll work directly with leadership and take ownership of the operational details that keep transactions and the organization moving.


Job Duties Include: 

- Coordinate financial transaction documentation, deadlines, and workflows
- Support entity formation and administration
- Coordinate with accounting, tax, appraisal, broker-dealer, and other outside partners
- Manage projects and follow-ups across multiple workstreams
- Help build efficient processes as the company grows

We are looking for a self-starter, resourceful, highly detail-oriented, dependable, and trusted with confidential information. You enjoy working independently and don't need constant direction to figure out what needs to happen next.

- This is not an accounting role. Financial knowledge is valuable, but operational execution, organization, judgment, and ownership are what will make someone successful.
- Bachelors Degree Required
- Advanced computer skills required

100% remote flexibility. Direct access to leadership. Significant autonomy. Sophisticated transaction exposure without the traditional large-firm lifestyle.
